Watch face

Motion·by @itshassco·2026-08-25·inspora page·original post

What it is

Minimal analog watch face ('the most useless watch face'): a sparse dial with only 12/3/6/9 numerals and tick dots, thin black hour/minute hands and a red seconds hand that sweeps with a smooth (not ticking) motion; a side panel offers mode, style (Minimal/Classic?), color accents, and a 'Buy me a coffee' link.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-100%
Light grey dial, small tick marks + 4 numerals; hands at various positions across frames - red seconds hand sweeps continuously (visible at 9, 6, 3 positions), minute hand advances subtly; panel on left: MODE toggle (Analog), STYLE pills (Minimal...), color dots row (black, cream, yellow, white), 'SUNRISE/SUNSET'?, support link, 'CO'WATCH' footer. Numerals and ticks stay perfectly still - only hands move.

Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a minimal analog watch face ("the most useless watch face") - sparse dial with only 12/3/6/9 numerals and tick dots, thin black hour/minute hands and a red seconds hand that sweeps smoothly (no ticking). Side panel offers mode, style, color accents, and a "Buy me a coffee" link.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Light grey dial: small tick dots + numerals at 12/3/6/9 only. Thin black hour and minute hands; red seconds hand. Left panel: MODE toggle (Analog), STYLE pills (Minimal...), color dot row (black, cream, yellow, white), support link, footer.

## Motion spec
Pattern: real-time clock.
- Seconds hand: smooth continuous sweep, 60s/rev, linear - derived from milliseconds, not stepped per second.
- Minute/hour hands: advance continuously at true rate.
- Optional "mechanical" style: seconds hand steps per second with a slight overshoot spring.
- Dial, numerals, panel: perfectly still.

## Calibration
- The smooth sweep is the entire aesthetic - a ticking seconds hand breaks it (unless the mechanical style is explicitly chosen).
- Hand lengths: seconds longest and thinnest; hour short and slightly thicker; classic proportions.
- Red seconds hand is the only color accent on the dial.

## Reduced motion
Hands show real time but update once per second without continuous sweep.

## Don't miss
- Angles come from actual time including milliseconds - no setInterval(1000) stepping.
- transform-origin exactly at the dial center; a 1px offset wobbles visibly at the tip.
- Sparse dial (4 numerals, dot ticks) - do not fill in 1-11.
